Bibrka Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Bibrka, Ukraine

Not demolished. NOTE: the source data contains a direct conflict on this cemetery's condition - the structured 'demolished' field says 'no,' while the narrative text separately states 'Presumably, it was demolished during and after WWII.' Both are reported here rather than silently resolved. This cemetery was marked on Austro-Hungarian military survey maps from the 1860s and 1880s. Jews are first recorded in Bibrka in 1625, reaching 713 by 1765, mostly in commerce and crafts; a boys' school opened in 1788. Rabbi Simche ben Yaacov, a leader of Galician Hasidism, was active here from 1800-1830. Population reached 1,778 (63%) by 1859 and 2,500 (47%) by 1900; the Zionist society Ahavath Zion formed in the late 19th century, and tzadik Yithok-Aizik Lenner of Stratin lived here from 1910, when seven synagogues and four charity organizations operated. Population reached 1,480 (34%) by 1921. The Wehrmacht captured Bibrka June 30, 1941; a locally organized pogrom killed 60 Jews within days. A July 1941 ghetto held nearly 3,600; over 1,500 were deported to Belzec by late 1942, and the remaining population was executed at the cemetery of nearby Volove on April 13, 1943. About 40 Jews returned after the war.
